ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Preventing mediator release

A laboratory exposes sensitized mast cells to an allergen and measures histamine in the surrounding medium. Pretreatment with cromolyn reduces mediator release compared with an untreated control culture. Which action best explains the preventive effect demonstrated in this experiment?

  1. Blockade of muscarinic receptors on airway smooth muscle
  2. Neutralization of circulating IL-5
  3. Irreversible inhibition of cyclooxygenase in platelets
  4. Inhibition of mast-cell degranulation
  5. Direct stimulation of beta-2 receptors
Answer and explanation

Inhibition of mast-cell degranulation

Cromolyn stabilizes mast cells and limits release of mediators rather than acting as a direct bronchodilator.

Option explanations

Inhibition of mast-cell degranulation: Cromolyn stabilizes mast cells and limits release of mediators rather than acting as a direct bronchodilator.

Direct stimulation of beta-2 receptors: That is the action of beta-2 agonists.

Blockade of muscarinic receptors on airway smooth muscle: That describes antimuscarinic bronchodilators.

Neutralization of circulating IL-5: That describes anti-IL-5 biologics.

Irreversible inhibition of cyclooxygenase in platelets: That is unrelated to cromolyn’s mast-cell effect.
